utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you all. And in my case, at least, welcome back for the new year. We have today a short Status Conference in respect of the two accused men, Cermak and Markac. Somebody has plugged in something or unplugged something. We have a great deal of feedback. That's better. Thank you. The two accused are on pre-trial release and they have been excused from attendance today. They are represented by their counsel. Mr. Whiting, you appear for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon, Your Honour. It's a pleasure to see you again and on behalf of the Prosecution, happy new year. I appear on behalf of the Prosecution with Ms. Laurie Sartorio, to my immediate right, Ms. Katherine Gallagher, and our case manager, Ms. Lakshmie Walpita.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Whiting. Mr. Prodanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague, Mrs. Jadranka Slokovic and I are appearing here on behalf of General Cermak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Separovic? It's Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Goran Mikulicic, appearing on behalf of Mr. Markac. Mr. Separovic remained in Zagreb and will be available via the videolink. I would like to extend my best wishes for the new year. At this point in time, I'm representing Mr. Markac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This had been planned to be a more significant Status Conference. One had to be called at about this time, of course, because of the requirement of the Rule that requires a Status Conference at least every 120 days, but there have been filed a significantly amended indictment and it had been intended that the two accused men would plead again to that amended indictment. But overtaking that, just about at the time that the Tribunal adjourned for the vacation, the circumstance arose that General Gotovina came into the custody of the Tribunal, and the nature of the case against him and the cases against the two Accused, Mr. Cermak and Mr. Markac, are quite closely related and the Prosecution has indicated that it intends that it will move to join the cases so that all three might be tried together. Now, the Prosecution has not filed that motion yet, but it has indicated one can be expected shortly and during this month, as I understand it. Very clearly, the question of joinder can affect a great deal everything that is being done in respect of the preparation for trial of these two Accused. So that it is, I think, quite obvious to all counsel, as it is to the Chamber, that it is desirable that the question of joinder be dealt with as quickly as possible so that we can know whether we are preparing a case for the trial of three Accused or of two Accused, and that being so, it occurred to the Chamber that it would be premature at this point, for example, to have General Cermak and Markac plead to this new indictment because if there is to be a joinder of General Gotovina, there will be necessarily yet a further indictment, one which includes him. There may be little change to the allegations against Cermak and Markac or there may be more substantial change. I don't know. But whichever way it goes, clearly, it seemed unnecessary to bring the two Accused from their country to The Hague to plead to the indictment as it now stands today before we know whether there will be yet a further indictment. So for that reason, we will not proceed today with the pleas that were intended and hence there is no need for the attendance of the two Accused. But that, of course brings into focus the importance of the Prosecution and its proposal for joinder. Do I correctly understand, Mr. Whiting, that there will be a motion for joinder that can be expected in the very near future?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Phrased like that, I can say yes. And I'll explain why I say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's the art of counsel, to phrase a question that gets a --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The correct answer. To be clear, it will be primarily a motion for joinder but there will also be an aspect of amendment of indictment also, and that's particularly true not with respect to this indictment but with respect to the indictment against Mr. Gotovina, which has not been updated the way the indictment in this case has been updated. There may also be a slight tinkering with -- but I don't think it's more than that, with this indictment. Now, the -- with respect to the timing it's our -- we are aiming to have it filed by the end of the month. However, one other consequence of the change in this case, and the rest of Mr. Gotovina is that -- and the fact that I have started a trial in another case is that there may be a shift in the personnel on the -- on behalf of the OTP in this case and there may be another STA who will be handling the case. That's being decided today or maybe Monday. For that reason, I would just add this caveat, that our goal of filing by the end of the month might slip by no more than one week in order to allow whoever the new STA is on the case a chance to at least read the motion, the joinder indictment, the amendments to the indictment and so forth. So our goal remains to file it by the end of the month. However, that goal might slip by one week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Whiting. We will await with interest what might develop there. Could I simply emphasise that really nothing of practical substance can occur in respect of the two present Accused until we have and can deal with this question of joinder because almost everything else can be affected by the consequences should joinder be ordered. So if we are to move this case along and have it ready for trial, as in the case of both Cermak and Markac would be their anxiety, given that they have been in custody here for quite sometime and now are on pre-trial release, that it would be of importance that attention be given quickly to the question of joinder, which is foreshadowed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, there are no pending motions before the Chamber, and we can turn to the matters of disclosure just so that we can confirm the present position. Since the last conference, there have been some further disclosure made pursuant to Rule 66, as I understand it, Mr. Whiting. Perhaps you could quickly indicate the present position.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, there has been additional disclosure pursuant to Rule 66 and there is also been some -- a number of transcript that is have been turned over. There were two matters that were raised at the 65 ter Conference yesterday which I'd like to try to see if we can offer a resolution to. The first is that Defence counsel indicated that they would like to have an indication from us which witness statements are disclosed pursuant to Rule 66(A)(ii), that is which are statements that we intend to use as witnesses. That list we are working on at the moment but what I proposed to Defence counsel, I spoke to them just before we convened here today is that next week we will provide to them a list of all of the witness statement that is we believe fall under 66(A)(ii). That moment is about 200 or 175. We are, as I've said, and as we said yesterday, working to pair down that list and sometime I expect that sometime in February, we will be able to provide a much paired down list of 66(A)(ii) witnesses to the Defence and we will do that. So that's the first matter is to indicate to them and give them a clear indication -- a clear understanding of which witnesses we believe to be under Rule 66(A)(ii). The second issue that was raised by Defence counsel is that because of the way we disclose -- we disclose in somewhat oftentimes in a bit of a piecemeal fashion because translations come in or statements come in, and we try in our disclosure letters and the attachments to make it as clear as possible how various documents relate to one another and how -- and how they are being disclosed. But I can understand the frustration of Defence counsel that at times that's hard -- it's hard to put it all together so what we are going to do is again by next week is we are going to provide to them a comprehensive log of all the disclosure that has occurred up to date so that they can see what they have received, how it matches up, which translations match up with which documents, and so forth. So I think that that addresses the issues and concerns with regard to disclosure that the Defence counsel raised yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Whiting. I can well understand that there might have been concern and confusion. Mr. Prodanovic, would what Mr. Whiting has indicated be of assistance to you in dealing with the problems that have been indicated?

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, certainly it would be of assistance on the meeting that we had yesterday, and also, today, just before the Status Conference, we agreed that there is a mechanism to resolve via this means the problem that exists in our communication. I think that this will be an appropriate mechanism.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Mikulicic is there anything you wish to add?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have nothing to add, Your Honour. Mr. Prodanovic presented the position which is supported by the Defence of Mr. Markac as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm grateful to counsel for that. And particularly, Mr. Whiting, to the Prosecution for what they are now proposing to deal with that matter. Rule 68, is there anything further you need to mention about the disclosure there? I know that what you've said deals with both 66 and 68.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes. To some -- yes, that's correct, Your Honour. I don't think there is anything further. I think there was some discussion about it at the 65 ter Conference. I think the parties are in agreement on how that is going to proceed. Of course, I can answer any questions if the Court has any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: In my mind, is whether there has been identified or whether you've got in place a procedure for identifying the fields of research in the computer records. It seemed that you had done some but you were awaiting further information from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. What we've done is we have done searches already across the system, and when I say across the system I mean across the entire collection which includes what's in the EDS and what's not in the EDS of the names of the Accused and that has unsurprisingly produced quite a large number of documents which we are now reviewing. And anything that comes -- that comes to our attention in the process of that review is being potential Rule 68 we will disclose under the Rules, under I guess it's 66(1) or (A), it's the first provision the actual knowledge provision. Beyond that we need to identify search terms to do further searches within -- and those further searches will be only within the non-EDS materials and those searches -- we will come up with search terms but we will also consult with the Defence about any proposed search terms. So we will share the search terms that we intend to use and ask for the input of the Defence if they have others that they would like us to search.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. So you anticipate no future problem with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I anticipate no future problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. While you're on your feet - I nearly got you - Rule 70 disclosure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes. We had thought at the last Status Conference there was only one outstanding collection. I had expected that that would be resolved by this date. It has not been. The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: One government, as I understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Exactly. A certain government to the north of here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Try west.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay. Northwest. I'm from the United States, our geography is very poor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Take pity on me. I'm from the southern hemisphere. Everything is different up here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm not going to say a word about that. To be fair it's a large number of documents and they are working on them. They are processing them, and they have indicated that they are working on it, they will be getting them back to us and we will disclose them as soon as we have them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Anything that either counsel for the Defence wish to raise about what Mr. Whiting has indicated or any other matter of disclosure? Nothing, Mr. Prodanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We have no additional issues or any other matters that have not been clarified concerning disclosure, and this is all based on our contacts with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Mikulicic, anything further?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No additional comments, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, I express my appreciation to counsel for what they've been able to work through and also the Senior Legal Officer at yesterday's hearing, in getting the matters of disclosure advanced and I look forward to that falling off this agenda. Agreed facts, Mr. Whiting?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That is one of the matters which is in some sense suspended now because of the possibility of a joinder. There has been some further developments. The Prosecution did respond to the response of the Defence counsel but I understand that in light of the potential for joinder, it doesn't make a lot of sense to finalise agreed facts or to go further because the counsel for Mr. Gotovina no doubt will have input on that. There may and few additional agreed facts. But I don't think -- once the joinder issue is resolved whichever which it's resolved, I don't think it will a long time to finalise the agreed facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I seem to have heard those words before.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: No doubt, you have. Probably from me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And I suspect I'll hear them again. Is there anything further, Mr. Whiting, that you would wish to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Not from the Prosecution, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Prodanovic any matter that you would wish to raise at this Status Conference.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mikulicic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no questions, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, thank you for those indications, counsel. We really are anxiously awaiting the matter of the motion for joinder so that that can be resolved one way or another so that we can then get back to serious preparation for trial. We can't let this preparation run along in an open-ended manner. We want to get the case ready for trial because there are possibilities for a trial during this coming year. I can't put it any higher than that, and it would be a pity for this case to miss out simply because we hadn't got it ready. It may not be number one on the list when a possibility for trial arises but I am anxious that at least it will be able to be ready and could therefore be fitted in if the opportunity arose. With that, we will now adjourn, and convene in due course when the motion for joinder arrives. Thank you.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
